output: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany criticizes UEFA's Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, arguing that they protect established elite clubs rather than preventing financial instability. Kompany believes these rules hinder newer teams from challenging the dominant clubs and cites Manchester City's success under Sheikh Mansour's ownership as an example of the positive impact such investments can have. He contends that FFP prevents smaller clubs with large fan bases, such as Leeds and Nottingham Forest, from competing at the highest levels of football.

Jeff Williams, a 26-year-old England Sevens international who has scored 36 tries on the World Series circuit, has signed with Bath for the upcoming season. Bath head coach Mike Ford is excited about Williams' addition, noting his dynamic playing style and fit with the team's attacking approach, while also praising his recruitment of young English talent. Williams, whose background includes playing in South Africa and France, brings valuable experience to the Aviva Premiership side.

Director David Ayer revealed the first full look at Jared Leto playing the Joker in "Suicide Squad," a film set to release on August 5, 2016, which will feature the iconic comic book villain without Batman. Leto transformed for the role by cutting his hair and shaving his face, marking him as the first actor to portray the character on the big screen since Heath Ledger. The film also stars Will Smith, Margot Robbie, and other anti-heroes and villains.

Three Florida corrections officers and a former officer trainee have been charged with plotting to kill a former inmate, according to the Florida Attorney General's office. They infiltrated a branch of the KKK and planned the murder after getting into a fight with the inmate, though the plot was foiled when the FBI staged a fake crime scene to make it appear the inmate had been killed. The suspects face up to 30 years in jail if convicted.

The conference call for Manny Pacquiao and Floyd Mayweather Jr. ahead of their fight was abruptly cancelled due to technical difficulties caused by a high number of participants. Pacquiao managed to answer just one question before the call was cut short, to which he replied that his training was going well. The call was rescheduled, with Mayweather set to have his own conference call the following day.

Serena Williams received a large cake to celebrate her 700th career victory at the Miami Open, following her victory over Sabine Lisicki. Meanwhile, Andy Murray also celebrated his 500th win with a cake. Despite the cake celebrations, Williams narrowly progressed to the semi-finals and will face Simona Halep in the next round.

Beijing International Airport is constructing the world's largest terminal, Terminal 1, to accommodate the dramatic rise in Chinese tourists traveling internationally. Designed by Zaha Hadid, the terminal will span 700,000 square meters and cater to 45 million passengers annually, aiming to enhance connectivity and reduce walking distances through its innovative design. This expansion reflects China's growing influence as a global traveler, with outbound tourism increasing from 10 million in 2000 to 109 million in 2014, spending $164 billion.

Manchester United's Wayne Rooney suffered a knee injury during their Premier League match against Everton, as confirmed by manager Louis van Gaal, who stated that the severity of the injury is yet to be determined. The defeat to Everton marked United's first back-to-back league losses under Van Gaal, causing them to slip to fourth place and potentially allowing Liverpool to close the gap in the race for Champions League qualification.

Manchester City is reportedly considering signing Jack Wilshere, who recently returned from an ankle injury and shared a humorous photo of his extensive supermarket haul on Instagram. The photo showcased Wilshere’s love for cereal, eggs, baked beans, and other staples, providing insight into his dietary needs for recovery. Wilshere humorously sought assistance from his followers to help him carry the weight of his shopping trip, joking about the challenge it posed.

A Venezuelan woman named Marleni Olivo threw a mango inscribed with her contact information at President Nicolas Maduro during a rally, an act that gained viral attention. In response, Maduro granted Olivo an apartment as part of his housing mission, addressing the issue she had raised. While Maduro's critics saw the incident as a potential political stunt, Olivo claimed her intention was simply to gain his attention to address her housing needs.

Carlos Tevez, a former striker for Manchester United and City, believes that scoring goals is harder in Serie A compared to the Premier League, despite having scored 36 goals in Italian league matches since joining Juventus in 2013. Tevez attributes the difference to the movement of the ball and less organized midfields in the Premier League, while acknowledging the high standard of play in Serie A. He also expresses confidence in Juventus' ability to compete at the highest level, including in the Champions League.

Jamie Carragher criticized Yaya Toure for allegedly ducking out of the way during a free-kick taken by Jason Puncheon, which secured Crystal Palace's victory and effectively ended Manchester City's hopes of salvaging a positive result. Carragher argued that Toure should have been more proactive in the wall formation, especially given his high salary and responsibilities as a key player. The incident contributed to Manchester City falling nine points behind leaders Chelsea in the Premier League standings.

A 50-year-old Australian man died after suffering a suspected heart attack at a hotel in Kuta, Bali, where he was on holiday. Witnesses reported that the man had complained of feeling unwell shortly before collapsing, though an autopsy was pending to confirm the cause of death. Kuta, known for its beaches and tourist attractions, remains a popular destination for Australian visitors despite the tragic incident.

Former Australian cricket captain and commentator Richie Benaud, who passed away at the age of 84 from skin cancer, was honored with a small, private funeral attended by his family and close friends in Sydney. Despite an offer from Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott for a state funeral, Benaud's widow, Daphne, declined in favor of a more intimate service. Benaud, known for his influential career both on and off the field, left behind a legacy cherished by cricket fans worldwide, with tributes continuing to be paid in his memory across Australia.

Isobel Attwood, a 16-year-old schoolgirl from Winchester, Hampshire, has been missing for two days and is believed to be with a man in his 20s in Southampton, according to friends' social media posts. Police are concerned for her welfare and believe she may be in the Winchester or Southampton areas, though they have not yet been able to locate her despite following up on several leads. Authorities are urging anyone with information to come forward and contact them.

If Manchester City fail to qualify for the Champions League this season, key players like Sergio Aguero, David Silva, Joe Hart, and Yaya Toure could lose out on a combined £6 million in bonuses. The team currently sits in fourth place, needing to avoid finishing fifth to secure their spot in the Champions League, with the top three qualifying automatically and the fourth-place team needing to win a qualifying round. Manchester City's poor recent form and financial constraints due to incentivized contracts put significant pressure on the team to achieve their European target.

Martin Skrtel, a Liverpool defender, has dismissed rumors linking him with moves to Wolfsburg and Napoli, stating he will remain with the Premier League club despite his contract expiring in 2016. His agent confirms they are finalizing a new contract, and there are no offers from German clubs. Despite Liverpool's poor season, Skrtel has reaffirmed his commitment to the team.

Cheryl Rios, a female CEO from Texas, sparked controversy by stating on Facebook that women should not be president due to their "hormones" preventing them from starting wars. Rios, who supports equal rights for men and women, faced criticism online, with many labeling her a misogynist. In response, Rios defended her right to hold and express such opinions, clarifying that she believes women can excel in other professions but not in the role of President.

Mario Mandzukic, despite suffering injuries in a physical Champions League match against Real Madrid, is expected to be fit for the return leg at the Bernabeu, according to Atletico Madrid's coach Diego Simeone. Simeone has confirmed that Mandzukic participated in training sessions and showed no signs of serious injury, positioning him as a likely starter alongside Antoine Griezmann in the upcoming match. Both players are in good form, with Griezmann scoring recently and Mandzukic recovering from his injuries.

Chelsea's Jose Mourinho spent the week preparing his team to face Marouane Fellaini, only to learn from a hotel doorman that Fellaini was not playing due to being there to pick up tickets from Eden Hazard. This led to confusion and a humorous moment where Mourinho identified the correct Fellaini from pictures on Google. Despite the misunderstanding, Fellaini did play and was effectively man-marked by Kurt Zouma in the 1-0 win for Chelsea, who moved closer to securing the Premier League title.

Dawn Milosky, a 45-year-old woman from Beachwood, New Jersey, was involved in a severe accident where her car overturned and caught fire. She was found unconscious in her 2006 Toyota Solara convertible by responding police officers who quickly freed her; she required medical intervention including defibrillation and CPR before being airlifted to a hospital. Milosky faces charges including driving while intoxicated and reckless driving.

A farmer in eastern China has become famous for owning a six-legged goat, nicknamed the "spider goat" by internet users. Born to two normal goats, the unusual kid, which initially had six legs of similar length, now has four functional legs and two that are shorter and cannot touch the ground. The farmer plans to let the goat grow naturally without attempting to remove the extra legs.

West Ham United is considering signing Javier Hernández from Real Madrid as part of their summer recruitment plan. The 26-year-old striker, known as "The Little Pea," will leave Real Madrid at the end of the season and could be available for around £7 million due to not being in Louis van Gaal's plans. Alongside this, West Ham is also targeting several younger players including Pedro Obiang, Moussa Konate, and Fabian Schar.

Stuart McCall, the manager of Rangers, has dismissed any thoughts of his future at the club being decided before the end of the season, emphasizing that while the team has recently won three consecutive matches and restored some positivity to the club, they have not yet achieved anything significant in the Championship. McCall insists that he will not engage in any meaningful discussions with the Ibrox board regarding his contract until after the play-offs. Additionally, Shane Ferguson, who was involved in a controversial loan deal with Newcastle United, is expected to join Rangers next week, though McCall is cautious about Ferguson's immediate availability due to a long-term knee injury.

Werder Bremen secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Hamburg SV in a crucial match, thanks to an 84th-minute penalty by Franco Di Santo, which kept Bremen's hopes for a Europa League spot alive. Despite new coach Bruno Labbadia's return to Hamburg, the match ended with Hamburg in last place, while Bremen moved up to seventh. With five matches remaining, Labbadia faces the challenge of preventing Hamburg, the only team never to have played in the second division, from experiencing relegation for the first time.

A two-year-old boy fell into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after slipping between a 10 to 12-foot gap in the railing while being held by his parents; the child was quickly rescued by his parents and treated for minor injuries at the hospital without any interaction with the cheetahs. The zoo plans to press child endangerment charges against the family responsible, and the exhibit was closed following the incident. Visitors described the parents' actions as shocking and dangerous, with some suggesting the parents may have been dangling the child over the railing.

Russian TV channel TV Rain gave Hillary Clinton's campaign video an 18+ rating due to concerns it might violate Russia's anti-gay propaganda law. The video included a brief scene of a gay couple holding hands, prompting the channel to avoid potential legal issues. This decision reflects the uncertainty surrounding the interpretation of the law, which bans "propaganda of nontraditional sexual relations" around minors, and follows similar actions taken in response to previous controversial content.

Siem de Jong, Newcastle United's 26-year-old midfielder, made a comeback by playing 45 minutes for the Under 21 team after recovering from a collapsed lung, though his performance suggested he may not be ready for the upcoming match against Tottenham. Meanwhile, Facundo Ferreyra, another loan signing, substituted de Jong at halftime but has yet to make his senior debut due to injuries. Derby County secured their victory with goals from Alefe Santos and Farrend Rawson in the second half.

Chef Ally Lees of Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a massive omelette weighing 12,000 calories and measuring three feet in circumference for an Easter promotion. The omelette, made from 150 eggs, is so large that it requires at least five people to finish it and contains 16 times the recommended daily protein intake for a man. Despite its size and caloric content, Chef Ally found the taste enjoyable but acknowledged the potential health risks associated with such a high-protein meal.

Three London 2012 Olympic gold medalists—Jessica Ennis-Hill, Mo Farah, and Greg Rutherford—will participate in the Sainsbury’s Anniversary Games at the Olympic Stadium this summer. The event, which features a two-day Diamond League meeting and the IPC Athletics Grand Prix Final, is set to take place from July 24-26 and aims to recreate the excitement of the 2013 games. Ticket sales have begun, with prices ranging from £10 to £20 for adults and concessions.

In Rio de Janeiro, a popular snack bar was found to be using the meat of stray dogs, killed with blows to the head, to make pastels, a traditional Brazilian pastry. The owner, Chinese Van Ruilonc, admitted to using the dogs, claiming they were strays collected from the streets. This discovery came alongside the investigation of alleged slave-like conditions for Chinese workers at the establishment, revealing a cage where they were confined and forced to work long hours without pay.

Ebony Dickens, using a pseudonym on Facebook, posted a threat to shoot every white cop she sees, which led to her arrest by local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. The controversial post detailed planned killings and specifically targeted white officers, prompting a serious response from law enforcement who obtained a search warrant at her home, finding a firearm and multiple computers. Dickens was charged with disseminating information related to terrorist acts and released on a $10,000 bond after appearing in court.

PSV Eindhoven won the Dutch Eredivisie championship for the first time in seven seasons by defeating Heerenveen 4-1, securing 79 points and leaving Ajax Amsterdam behind in second place. Key to PSV's victory were two headed goals by Luuk de Jong and a stunning free-kick from Memphis Depay. Meanwhile, Dordrecht's loss to Vitesse Arnhem brought them closer to relegation, while AZ Alkmaar secured a place in the Europa League playoffs with a 3-1 win over ADO Den Haag.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva was reportedly beaten to death by his head teacher, Lalit Verma, at Dwarika Prasad School in Railamau village, India, after being accused of stealing another student's pencil and eraser. The severe beating led to Shiva's immediate death upon arrival at the hospital due to internal bleeding. This incident has sparked further investigations into the use of corporal punishment by teachers in Indian schools, as similar cases of children dying under similar circumstances have been reported across the country.

A gastrointestinal illness affecting 100 passengers and five crew members has broken out on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship, which is currently 2,117 passengers strong. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is investigating the cause of the illnesses but has not yet determined a specific origin. In response, the ship's operators have increased cleaning efforts and are cooperating with the CDC for further testing.

Loren Mathieson captured her Boston Terrier, Gizmo, performing an impressive "paw-stand" walking trick after he put on new booties. The video shows Gizmo taking steps, then lifting his hind legs off the ground to walk in a vertical position before reaching his owner, who is seen laughing. The clip has garnered over 80,000 views and brought joy to many viewers.

New Orleans has implemented a city-wide smoking ban, which took effect on Wednesday at midnight, prohibiting smoking in most public places such as bars, casinos, and restaurants. Despite some opposition from bar owners and smokers who feared revenue losses, the ban was passed unanimously by the city council in January. The ban includes fines starting at $50, and a legal challenge from some bar owners and casino operators remains pending in state court.

Manchester United secured a crucial victory over West Ham United in the Under 21 Premier League, moving four points clear at the top of the table. Despite taking an early lead through Reece Oxford, West Ham fell behind as Josh Harrop equalized, followed by Joe Rothwell's goal. In a match dominated by Manchester United's attacking prowess, led by captain Adnan Januzaj, the score remained level until Jordan Brown equalized just before halftime. However, Harrop scored again in the second half, securing the win for Manchester United.

The Archbishop of Brisbane, Phillip Aspinall, has joined a local Catholic priest in advocating for the removal of Queensland's 'gay panic' homicide defense from the state's common law. This legal defense can reduce murder charges to manslaughter if the defendant claims they felt threatened sexually. Aspinall emphasized that violence is never a justified response to unwanted sexual advances and used this stance to appeal against other forms of violence, including those seen in recent anti-Islam rallies and church vandalism in Melbourne.

Sandra Bullock has been named the world's most beautiful woman by People magazine for 2015, marking her as the oldest woman to receive this honor. In an interview, Bullock downplayed the accolade, emphasizing character traits such as being a good person and mother over physical appearance. The cover story also highlights her family life with her son and her approach to maintaining health and happiness beyond her 40s.

An improvised bomb exploded near a U.N. vehicle in Garowe, Somalia, on Monday morning, killing six people, including four UNICEF aid workers, and wounding several others. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack, which targeted U.N. staff members as they traveled to work. In another incident, three African Union troops were killed in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region, also claimed by Al-Shabaab.

Gary Saurage, a wildlife park owner in Beaumont, Texas, was called to capture a 400-pound, 11-foot-long alligator from a family's backyard pond using only his bare hands. The alligator, which proved to be particularly aggressive, was successfully removed and taken to Saurage’s park. This incident highlights the ongoing challenge of managing alligator populations in residential areas while emphasizing the importance of maintaining safe distances from these animals.

In eastern Turkey, five members of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) were killed and one injured in a clash with Turkish forces, while four Turkish soldiers were also wounded. Turkish officials, including Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoğlu and President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, condemned the attack and vowed a strong response. This incident occurred against the backdrop of calls from jailed PKK leader Abdullah Öcalan for his fighters to cease violence and engage in peace talks.

Two 18-month-old twin boys tragically died after accidentally falling into a canal in Yuma, Arizona, on Friday morning. The boys were found in the water around two hours after the incident by a Border Patrol helicopter, and though emergency services provided immediate care, they were pronounced dead upon arrival at the hospital. The area near the canal is frequently used by families, but no foul play is suspected in the tragedy.

Orlando City, a Major League Soccer team, has shown interest in signing Javier Hernández, the Mexican international forward who has struggled during his loan at Real Madrid. Despite competition from eight European clubs, including teams like Southampton and Wolfsburg, Hernández could find a new home with Orlando City, given their strong Latin-American fanbase. Additionally, Manchester United has revised their contract offer to teenage midfielder Andreas Pereira, whose father has received interest from several European clubs should Pereira choose to leave United.

Joel Burger, 24, proposed to his girlfriend Ashley King, also 23, and they plan to get married under the name Burger-King. The couple, who have been friends since kindergarten, intend to serve drinks in personalized Burger King cups at their wedding, adding a fun twist to their nuptials. Their unique relationship began in fifth grade when a motivational speaker coined their combined names as "Burger King," a nickname they have embraced throughout their relationship.

A secret police intelligence report from 1964 revealed that a hit band from the 1960s, along with notorious BBC DJ Jimmy Savile, frequented a notorious pedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London. This information emerged as part of Operation Yewtree, an investigation initiated in 2013 after a woman came forward in 2003 to report her abuse by Savile in the 1970s. Detective Superintendent David Grey noted that while the police had intelligence linking both Savile and the band to the brothel, this alone did not provide sufficient grounds to investigate further without the benefit of hindsight.

Sadie, a German Shepherd from Alberta, Canada, has been captured on camera using her nose to turn on an electric organ and sit down to play piano sonatas. Despite her owner suggesting she may have made a mistake, Sadie continues with her performance, which is documented in a viral video viewed over 12,000 times. The video showcases Sadie's musical talent and cleverness, having learned to play the piano after being adopted from an animal rescue shelter in 2009.

A phone thief named Ivan Balashov took a selfie in a Russian smartphone shop before stealing a preferred model, but was caught when police recognized him from the picture. After selecting a handset and attempting to leave the store, Balashov was stopped by security and later fled with the stolen phone, selling it shortly afterward. Police identified him based on the selfie taken in the shop and sentenced him to a three-month suspended sentence.

A new documentary trailer for Amy Winehouse's life and music has been released, set for UK release on July 3rd. The film, titled "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name," aims to capture both the artist and the personal aspects of Winehouse's life, including her struggles with fame and substance abuse. The documentary includes extensive, previously unseen footage and audio, and has been endorsed by Winehouse's family, who hope it will serve as a tribute to her musical legacy.

The article suggests watching "The Big Bang Theory" on Thursday for an episode featuring the return of Christine Baranski and Laurie Metcalf as the show's characters' mothers. It also recommends tuning in to "Saturday Night Live" hosted by Scarlett Johansson on Saturday, and "Mom" on Thursday for its Emmy-worthy performances. Additionally, the article highlights other shows including "Backstrom," "Blue Bloods," and "Younger," which have upcoming finales or new seasons.

The hit British show Downton Abbey, which will conclude its run later this year, might see some of its beloved characters return in a new American adaptation titled "The Gilded Age." Created by Downton Abbey's original writer, Julian Fellowes, the new series will be set in 19th-century New York and features characters like the Dowager Countess Violet and the Earl and Countess of Grantham, portrayed by Dame Maggie Smith and Elizabeth McGovern respectively, in their younger versions. NBC is optimistic about the project and hopes to bring it to air as early as September.

Steven Gerrard is set to start for Liverpool in their FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley, marking what could be his final game at the national stadium before joining LA Galaxy. Manager Brendan Rodgers has selected Gerrard despite using him sparingly this season, praising his importance in big matches. Gerrard, who served a three-match ban, hopes to end his illustrious career with a trophy, having last won the FA Cup in 2006 and the League Cup in 2012.

A new Dr. Seuss book, "What Pet Should I Get?", has generated significant interest, leading to an increased first printing from 500,000 to 1 million copies to meet demand. This release marks the first original Dr. Seuss book since 1990 and features characters from his classic "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish." The book, which was written between 1958 and 1962 but remained undiscovered until recently, is expected to debut on July 28, 2023.

Jessica Carey surprised her grandmother, Patty Lawing, during a visit by having a tattoo of Patty as a young woman inked on her arm and bringing her grandchildren along for the surprise. Captured on video, Patty Lawing was overwhelmed and emotional upon seeing the tattoo, which was based on a childhood portrait. Jessica had arranged for the tattoo and organized the visit specifically to catch the reaction on camera, sharing the touching moment online only recently.

At 65 years old, Annegret Raunigk, a German primary school teacher, is set to give birth to quadruplets, making her the oldest known woman to carry and deliver such a high number of babies. This pregnancy, conceived through 18 months of fertility treatment, comes after she previously gave birth to her youngest daughter at age 55. Her physician notes that while her age poses risks, her current pregnancy is progressing well, though they are closely monitoring her health.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, plans to send an unmanned rover to the moon by 2018, aiming to develop soft-landing technologies potentially applicable to future manned missions to the moon or Mars. This mission, which could cost between $83.4 million and $125 million, involves using a smart lander equipped with face recognition software to identify craters. The move reflects Japan's efforts to catch up with China and India, which have also made significant strides in lunar exploration.

Three Brazilian football players, including Corinthians striker Paolo Guerrero, have been diagnosed with dengue fever, forcing them to miss important matches and prompting Brazilian clubs to take preventive measures against mosquito bites. The outbreak, which has caused over 460,000 cases in Brazil in 2015, has led to increased vigilance among teams and players who are taking steps such as using insect repellent and avoiding practices during peak mosquito hours. Clubs are also cooperating with health officials to inspect and control potential breeding sites for the mosquitoes that transmit the disease.

Manchester United striker James Wilson, when interviewed, expressed his desire to adopt Wayne Rooney's free-kick-taking ability, praising Rooney's daily practice and accuracy. Wilson also highlighted his admiration for Robin van Persie’s movement and Radamel Falcao’s instincts in the penalty box, noting that these qualities could significantly enhance his own game. This aspiration stems from Wilson’s opportunity to train with experienced forwards and learn from their skills, as he has made 16 appearances for Manchester United this season, scoring two goals.

In Milwaukee, Wisconsin, Archie Brown Jr., who struck and killed a 2-year-old child with his van, was subsequently shot and killed by an unknown assailant at the scene. A 15-year-old boy was also shot and later died, though his connection to the incident is unclear. The shooting may be considered a possible act of revenge, as suggested by a local alderman, who emphasized that such issues should be resolved without resorting to violence.

A child from Memphis, Tennessee, has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers by posting pictures of himself in gang-related activities, including posing with guns and drugs, and using sexually explicit language. His tweets have sparked criticism from the public and authorities, who are concerned about the potential long-term impact on the child. Despite the backlash, the child has defended his actions, citing personal hardships and expressing frustration with those who criticize him.

John Schumann, former frontman of Redgum, expressed disappointment after his song "I Was Only 19" was used at Reclaim Australia rallies aimed at opposing Islamic law in Australia. The song, intended to promote compassion and inclusiveness, was co-opted by a "confused 'patriotic' movement," according to Schumann. Violence erupted during the nationwide protests, resulting in several arrests and minor injuries.

Emmanuel Adebayor, a forward for Tottenham Hotspur, has denied reports of his potential transfer and affirmed his commitment to staying with the club. Despite a recent underwhelming performance and the emergence of Harry Kane as a key player, Adebayor continues to express his gratitude for playing in the Premier League and plans to fight for his place in the team. However, his form has notably declined since joining in 2011, making him a less prominent figure in the squad.

Stuart Pearce advocates for maintaining Manuel Pellegrini as Manchester City's manager despite the team's recent poor performance and challenges in securing a top-four finish. Pearce attributes the team's struggles partly to the declining influence of key player Yaya Toure and advises that the squad needs significant strengthening in the summer. Despite the team's dejected appearance, particularly during losses like the recent derby against Manchester United, Pearce hopes Pellegrini remains in charge to guide the club towards improvement.

Steve Bruce remains optimistic about keeping Hull City in the Barclays Premier League despite their recent 2-0 defeat to Southampton, which left them struggling to avoid relegation. Bruce attributes their difficulties to several long-term injuries to key players and believes that securing nine or eight more wins could secure their place in the league. Despite upcoming challenging matches against top teams like Liverpool and Arsenal, Bruce insists that his team is up for the challenge and confident in their ability to survive.

In Reading, a full-scale terror alert was triggered when a passer-by reported a suspicious object on a barge sailing down the Thames, which appeared to be a guided missile launcher with a dummy in a balaclava nearby. Upon investigation by Thames Valley Police and an Army bomb disposal team, the "weapon" was confirmed to be a harmless dummy and a decorative model, not a real explosive device. Local residents criticized the prank as irresponsible and potentially dangerous given the sensitive security situation in the area.

Tiger Woods suffered an unusual injury during his play at the Masters when his club struck a tree root on the ninth hole, causing him to yelp in pain. Despite the setback, Woods was able to continue playing and finished the tournament at 5-under-par, marking his best performance in over a year. He humorously noted that he had to pop a ligament in his right wrist back into place to continue playing, although it was still sore.

Iker Casillas, who has dedicated his entire career to Real Madrid, declares his intention to stay with the club despite potential competition from Manchester United's David de Gea. Casillas, a 33-year-old veteran, emphasizes his commitment to earning the starting goalkeeper position through hard work and dedication. Casillas focuses on helping Real Madrid defend their Champions League title, expressing confidence in their ability to overcome strong opponents in the upcoming semi-finals.

A video has surfaced showing a failed missile launch of an S300 rocket in Russia, where the rocket barely managed to lift off before falling back to the ground, causing a small explosion and debris. This embarrassing incident occurred shortly after another rocket launch killed six Russian missile technicians in Ukraine, despite attempts by officials to keep the details under wraps. These incidents have likely caused embarrassment for President Vladimir Putin, given the significant increase in the Russian defense budget under his leadership.

Lancashire County Cricket Club has signed Australian all-rounder James Faulkner as their overseas player for much of this summer, replacing Peter Siddle. Faulkner, who recently won the World Cup with Australia, will join the team after completing his commitments in the Indian Premier League. The club expresses great excitement about Faulkner's addition, praising his world-class status and potential benefits to both his career and the team's performance.

In 1996, Mary Kay Letourneau, a 34-year-old teacher, had an affair with her 13-year-old student, leading to her imprisonment and the birth of a child with him. After serving over seven years, she was released in 2005 and married her former lover, Vili Fualaau, celebrating their 10th wedding anniversary in 2015. In an upcoming interview with ABC's "20/20," the couple will discuss how they maintain their marriage despite their significant age difference and personal struggles, including Letourneau's plans to teach again and efforts to lift her sex offender status.

Former Liverpool footballer Jamie Carragher traveled to Spain during the international break to support his son James, who was playing for the Liverpool Under-12s in the Mediterranean International Cup. Carragher documented his experience by posting a picture from the opening ceremony on Instagram and later watched as his son's team drew 1-1 against a local Catalan side. The prestigious tournament, now in its 15th year, has featured many renowned players including Lionel Messi and Neymar in its earlier editions.

Seattle-based filmmaker Gabriel Ng spent three months in Thailand, creating a stunning six-minute video that showcases the country's natural beauty and cultural sites using a drone-mounted camera. Filmed primarily on the island of Ko Samui, the video captures breathtaking coastal vistas, religious landmarks, and scenes of daily life, earning praise for its high-definition quality and capturing the essence of Thai tourism. This project follows previous work by Ng using drones for aerial filming, including weddings and famous U.S. landmarks.

Peter Moores, the current England coach, insists he can work with Michael Vaughan if he becomes the new director of cricket, despite their past disagreements. Moores believes the new role should not necessitate an additional voice in the dressing room, depending on how the position is defined. Despite the impending changes in management, Moores remains focused on his role and is optimistic about the future, particularly with the emergence of promising young players.

Nottingham Forest intends to pursue a transfer for Blackburn's striker Jordan Rhodes, valued at £10 million, with the hope that a direct cash offer will succeed where previous attempts failed. Blackburn manager Gary Bowyer anticipates further interest in Rhodes' strike partner, Rudy Gestede, after Gestede scored 19 goals, including one against Forest. Several clubs, including Hull, Crystal Palace, West Brom, and Southampton, have shown interest in Gestede.

In a heartwarming scene captured in North Carolina, three dogs—a Husky named Sky and two Springer Spaniels named Sadie and Marshall—formed a unique musical ensemble by barking and howling in harmony. Starting with Sadie's bark, followed by Sky's melodious howl and Sadie's mimicry, the trio eventually harmonized, creating a surprisingly musical performance despite the unconventional instrument. The dogs continued their impromptu concert until their owner called for them to stop, leaving the dogs looking surprised and slightly disappointed.

French climber Alain Robert, nicknamed the 'French Spiderman,' scaled the 1,007-foot Cayan Tower in Dubai without a safety harness, using only sticky tape and chalk for assistance, taking about an hour and a half to reach the top. This daring feat, captured on video, is part of a series of climbs he has undertaken worldwide, though he has faced legal troubles and bans in various cities. Robert previously climbed the world's tallest building, the 2,717-foot Burj Khalifa, in 2011, adhering to safety regulations despite his usual no-harness approach.

An experimental cancer drug previously discarded due to poor results has shown promise in reversing the effects of Alzheimer's disease in mice, according to researchers at Yale University. The drug, AZD0530, works by blocking a process that damages nerve connections in the brain responsible for storing memory. Scientists are now launching human trials to test its effectiveness in Alzheimer's patients, with initial results indicating restored memory and reduced inflammation in treated animals.

Marvel Studios has revealed the appearance of the Vision, played by Paul Bettany, in the upcoming "Avengers: Age of Ultron" sequel, putting an end to months of speculation. As part of the superhero trend, Netflix debuted a video of Charlie Cox in his Daredevil suit for the new series "Daredevil." Additionally, director Bryan Singer announced that Ben Hardy would play the role of Angel in the upcoming "X-Men: Apocalypse" film, along with images of Jamie Bell's character The Thing from the rebooted "Fantastic Four" movie, confirming his appearance.

Veteran referee Kenny Bayless, who has worked with both Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao extensively, will officiate their high-profile fight, earning $25,000 for the job. However, former opponent Oscar De La Hoya argues that Bayless's familiarity with Mayweather gives him an unfair advantage, citing instances where Bayless broke up clinches in Mayweather's favor. Despite this criticism, Bayless remains one of the top referees in the sport.

Harry Kane's participation in the upcoming Under-21 European Championship is uncertain due to Tottenham Hotspur's scheduled post-season friendly in Malaysia. The club's manager, Mauricio Pochettino, is concerned about the striker's risk of burnout and wants him to rest adequately before the start of the new season. Despite Kane's desire to play for England, the FA is in discussion with Tottenham about potentially excluding him from the tournament to ensure he has sufficient recovery time.

A measles outbreak affecting over 130 people in California, linked to visits to Disney theme parks, has been declared over by the California Department of Public Health after 42 days without new cases. The majority of those infected (70%) were found to be unvaccinated, according to the state's investigation. Public health measures such as prompt case investigation, vaccination of at-risk individuals, and increased awareness among healthcare providers were instrumental in controlling the outbreak.

In San Miguel de Tucuman, Argentina, police are searching for a family of six who were photographed riding on a single motorbike without helmets, with two adults and four children aboard. This incident follows a similar case in Junin where a family of seven was also captured on camera using the same method of transportation. Both incidents have drawn widespread condemnation from the public and authorities, who have urged anyone recognizing the families to come forward.

A 44-year-old woman named Andrea McVeigh was severely injured when she was struck by a cyclist while walking on the pavement in Bermondsey, London. The cyclist fled the scene, prompting the woman’s husband to chase him. The incident left McVeigh scarred for life with multiple facial and hand injuries. Police are now issuing CCTV footage of the cyclist in hopes of identifying and arresting the individual responsible for the shocking and callous attack.

A headstone marking the burial site of Hillary Clinton's father, Hugh Rodham, was found tipped over in a cemetery in Scranton, Pennsylvania, just days after Clinton announced her candidacy for the presidency. The incident has sparked speculation and investigation; while some suspect vandalism, others consider weather conditions as a possible factor. The grave site, usually well-maintained by local resident Paul McGloin, who has tended to it since 1993, has drawn political attention due to its timing relative to Clinton's announcement.

A California woman, Beatriz Paez, was recording police activity when a U.S. marshal took her phone, smashed it with his foot, and kicked it away, causing her to feel unsafe. Paez has filed a complaint and is considering legal action against the marshals' actions, which were captured on video by another bystander. The U.S. Marshals Service is reviewing the incident, while a federal investigation has been requested due to the perceived illegality of the marshal's actions.

Max, a 18.5-inch tall corgi-Siberian husky cross, was found as a stray and has become a favorite at the Dogs Trust in Basildon, Essex. Despite his unique appearance and charming personality, Max has been abandoned and is now seeking a new home. The Dogs Trust suggests that the increasing popularity of wolf-like dog breeds, influenced by TV shows like Game of Thrones, has led to an increase in abandoned pets due to owners' underestimating the care required for these breeds.

Chilean pickpockets have emerged as the most effective thieves in central London, targeting wealthy tourists in areas such as the West End. An undercover police operation uncovered a gang of two Chilean women using burqas to target wealthy Arab tourists, with one bag containing €130,000, £20,000, and valuable jewelry. The police note that these organized gangs, which also include members from Romania, Algeria, and Bulgaria, use sophisticated tactics to avoid detection and operate across multiple European cities.

In a severe car crash near Southam, Warwickshire, a young driver survived a rollover and became trapped under his vehicle. Despite suffering head, chest, and leg injuries, the man remained conscious throughout the rescue operation, which took 25 minutes by firefighters using specialized cutting tools. Emergency services praised the quick response of a community paramedic who began treatment immediately upon arrival.

Fly-tippers have dumped an unprecedented 40 tonnes of industrial waste along the side of the road in the Suffolk village of Walsham-le-Willows, shocking local authorities and residents alike. Described as the worst case of flytipping in a police officer's 28-year career, the dumped waste, including materials from the carpet and veterinary industries, will cost thousands of pounds to remove. Authorities, alongside the National Farmers' Union and the Country Land and Business Association, are investigating the incident and working to prevent such environmental offenses in the future.

A man who refused to comply with security staff at Toronto's Pearson International Airport was tasered and brought to the ground, after he attempted to enter a restricted area despite being told he could not board a flight. The incident, captured on video by a bystander, shows the man mumbling and holding onto a black briefcase tightly while being tasered; he was later transferred to a hospital under Canada's Mental Health Act. Authorities decided to use non-lethal force considering the man's potential danger and the safety of the officers involved.

Serbia's President Tomislav Nikolic's government jet had to return to Belgrade after the co-pilot accidentally spilled coffee on the instrument panel, causing the plane to lose control and begin tumbling. The pilot managed to regain control and land safely, though the incident led to the cancellation of the president's planned meeting with Pope Francis. The co-pilot had his license suspended and admitted to activating the emergency slat button by mistake while trying to clean up the spill.

In South Africa, over 300 suspects have been arrested in connection with violent attacks against foreigners, which have forced thousands to seek refuge in temporary shelters. The government condemned these attacks and praised law enforcement for preventing further violence in cities like Durban. Despite the unrest, there has been an outpouring of support from South Africans who reject the xenophobic sentiment and remember the country's history of relying on African neighbors during times of hardship.

A skier named Zach Birnie captured harrowing footage of himself becoming caught in an avalanche while skiing off-piste in Revelstoke, Canada. Despite the heavy snow closing in around him and pushing him down the mountain, Birnie managed to emerge, though panting and shocked. Experts suggest that the fresh snow and steep terrain likely contributed to the avalanche, and recommend escaping the avalanche area, letting go of ski poles, opening bindings if possible, pulling knees to the chest, and holding arms in front of the face.

On the hottest day of the year, two bare-chested men in their 20s raided an Esso petrol station in Caterham, Surrey, forcing their way into the manager's office to look for cash but were caught on camera and fled when disturbed by staff. Police have released CCTV footage of the suspects and are appealing for public assistance in identifying them. A third man has been arrested and released on bail.

The Lada Niva 4x4, starting at £13,395 on the road, is gaining popularity as a replacement for the Land Rover Defender, despite being a subject of humor during the Soviet era. Known for its rugged design and durability, the Niva offers a more affordable alternative to luxury 4x4s, even available in a compact van format for £10,590. However, while the car’s simplicity and affordability are notable, its basic interior, which can easily be cleaned, might not appeal to those seeking luxury features.

A lawsuit has been filed against the nation's largest provider of HIV and AIDS medical care, the AIDS Healthcare Foundation, accusing it of a $20 million scam involving kickbacks to boost funding from Medicare and Medicaid across 12 states. The former managers allege that employees and patients received kickbacks for patient referrals, with some employees earning $100 bonuses for referring positive test results. Despite the allegations, the foundation maintains that it has not acted wrongly and argues that the federal government and state of Florida have declined to intervene in the case.

Liz, a bearded dragon owned by Shannen Hussein in Melbourne, has been filmed nodding her head in response to being asked if she is hungry, demonstrating what appears to be an understanding of human speech. Liz is rewarded with a superworm treat for her conversational skills, which she apparently enjoys very much. Shannen also owns a variety of other pets including a pet lamb named Winter, who has gained internet fame through Vine videos showcasing her playful antics.

A young man named Travis Hatfield from West Virginia became an internet sensation after posting a video of himself singing a George Jones song to his uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome. The video, which shows the two singing together weekly, has garnered over 410,000 views and showcases their passion for music. Travis, who dreams of becoming a country singer, is now receiving interest from Nashville record labels due to the viral video.

Nik Wallenda, the daredevil from the 'Flying Wallenda' family, plans to walk on an untethered high wire above the 400-foot Orlando Eye observation wheel in Florida, scheduled for April 29. The Orlando Eye, which will open to the public on May 4, consists of 30 air-conditioned glass capsules for visitors to enjoy the view. This stunt, though not the full circumference of the wheel, marks a significant challenge for Wallenda due to the larger size of the wheel and the absence of a safety pole.

Medhi Benatia, a central defender for Bayern Munich, is likely to miss both legs of the Champions League quarter-final against Porto due to a muscle injury sustained during a German Cup match. This injury, which could keep him out for two to four weeks, adds to an already lengthy list of injured players at Bayern Munich, including Bastian Schweinsteiger and David Alaba. Despite the setbacks, Bayern Munich remains competitive in all competitions, aiming for success in the Bundesliga, German Cup, and Champions League.

Bayern Munich defeated Porto 6-1 in the Champions League quarter-final second leg, advancing to the semi-finals under Pep Guardiola's tactical guidance. This victory adds to Bayern's impressive season with a total of 115 goals scored so far, and with five Bundesliga matches, the German Cup semi-final, and potential Champions League matches remaining, they could surpass 141 goals for the season if they maintain their current goal-scoring rate of 2.61 per game. The article highlights key moments from Bayern's recent games, showcasing the team's exceptional offensive performance.

Fernando Torres credits Diego Simeone as the key figure behind Atletico Madrid's recent success and their upcoming Champions League match against Real Madrid. Since Simeone's leadership, Atletico Madrid has become one of Europe's most respected teams, having not lost to Real Madrid in six matches since their 2014 Champions League final loss. Torres emphasizes that Simeone's focus on understanding the team's strengths and weaknesses is crucial to their competitive edge, despite lacking some of the star power of their rivals.

A light aircraft crash near Loch Etive in western Scotland led to the discovery of two bodies among the wreckage. The plane was last seen traveling from central Scotland to Tiree, one of the Inner Hebrides islands, and went missing around 30 miles east of Oban. Search and rescue efforts involved lifeboats, helicopters, and police, with the incident under investigation by the Procurator Fiscal.

A bus shattered the windscreen of a Boeing 777 passenger jet at Tashkent International Airport in Uzbekistan, causing significant damage but no known injuries; the busy airport, which handles the most passengers in Central Asia, experienced delays for numerous travelers. Such incidents are becoming increasingly frequent, including collisions between Ryanair planes at Dublin Airport and a British Airways plane hitting a hangar at Heathrow, both resulting in minimal injuries but substantial disruptions.

An off-duty Secret Service agent named Arthur Baldwin was arrested in Washington D.C. for attempting to break into a house and causing property damage, leading to the revocation of his security clearance and his placement on leave. This incident occurred just two days after a high-ranking supervisor was placed on leave amid accusations of misconduct, both of which have tarnished the Secret Service's reputation. Additionally, an investigation is ongoing regarding an incident in March where two senior agency officials were found in a restricted area of the White House following alcohol consumption.

Israel is developing a unique tunnelling detection system, designed to accurately identify tunneling activities from a distance using advanced sensors, which reportedly eliminates false alarms. This system, developed by Elbit Systems in collaboration with the Israeli Ministry of Defense, follows extensive consideration of over 700 proposals aimed at addressing tunnel threats. The system, expected to cost approximately £2.3 million per mile for installation, aims to enhance security along the Gaza-Israel border.

A primary school headteacher in south London has banned all drinks except water during school hours to promote long-term pupil health, but this decision has sparked a parental backlash. Parents argue that the ban is too strict and that children may go without drinking because they dislike water. The school defends the policy as part of a health initiative, though some critics view it as excessive.

Paul Smith has secured a high-profile fight against undefeated boxer Andre Ward on June 20 in Oakland, California. This match, though not for a world title, presents a significant challenge for Smith, who has been inactive since November 2013 and seeks to prove himself against one of the sport's top pound-for-pound fighters. Both fighters express enthusiasm for the bout, with Ward emphasizing the need to perform at his best due to Smith's potential to upset him.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel spent Easter on the island of Ischia in Italy, where she and her husband Joachim Sauer stayed at the five-star Miramare Spa Hotel despite the lack of sunshine. To stay active, Merkel hired a private Pilates instructor and focused on healthy vegetarian meals, while avoiding the hotel's pool area. Merkel's husband, a chemistry professor, largely kept to the background, as he typically does during their annual holiday together.

Ander Herrera, a Manchester United midfielder, has scored multiple goals without looking at the ball, including a brace against Aston Villa where his eyes were shut during both shots. This unusual goal-scoring habit has raised eyebrows, though it is not entirely new, as evidenced by his goal for Spain's Under 20 team in 2009. Despite his talent, Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal has advised him to improve his technique by controlling the ball before shooting.

A 23-month-old girl tragically died after her father accidentally struck her with a pickup truck in the driveway of their North Las Vegas home. The father and other family members were unaware that the toddler had wandered out from the house. The incident was ruled an accident, and no charges were filed.

The University of Connecticut baseball team has welcomed 5-year-old Grayson Hand, a child battling leukemia, as its newest member with the help of Team IMPACT. Grayson's involvement includes having his own locker and attending practices and games, while his sister Sophie was named an honorary cheerleader. This partnership symbolizes the broader support Grayson's family has received during his battle with cancer, emphasizing that the illness affects the entire family unit rather than just the individual patient.

A passenger on a London Midland train discovered excrement in a newspaper on the floor, causing severe delays and forcing the train to terminate early for cleaning. London Midland has vowed to provide police with CCTV footage of the suspect, while apologizing to affected passengers. This incident follows a similar event where a British Airways flight had to return to London due to a foul odor from an overflowing toilet.

James Rodriguez, who moved to Real Madrid from Monaco for £60 million, has become a key player for the team, winning 80% of games he starts in, according to Spanish newspaper Marca. Meanwhile, AS focuses on Cristiano Ronaldo's appeal following a yellow card for diving in a recent match, with a decision expected on his suspension for the next game. Additionally, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports that Inter Milan's coach Roberto Mancini plans to make significant summer signings, targeting eight players from a list of 21 candidates including several Premier League stars and other top players.

A Florida man named Kenneth Crowder, who was believed to be under the influence of Flakka, a powerful and dangerous drug, attacked a police officer after being shocked with a Taser twice, during which he claimed he was God and attempted to stab the officer with his own badge. Crowder was arrested and charged with battery on a law-enforcement officer, resisting with violence, and assault with a deadly weapon on a law-enforcement officer. Flakka, similar to a mix of crack cocaine and meth, can cause intense euphoria, hallucinations, and even apparent superhuman strength, leading to increased incidents of violent behavior among its users.

During a Russian Premier League match between Arsenal Tula and Torpedo Moscow, a brawl by Torpedo fans led to the suspension of the game for seven minutes. The fans broke down barriers, threw seats, and fought with law enforcement, forcing the referee to halt the match. Torpedo Moscow was later expected to face severe penalties for the incident, which was the fourth such occurrence involving the club this season.

High school girls in Huizhou, China, are undergoing military-style dagger drill training as part of their self-defense program under the guidance of a former special forces soldier. These girls, aged between 16 and 18, practice with non-harmful knives that have retractable blades to ensure safety, learning eight movements that could help them fend off attackers using any sharp object available. The training, which includes shouting combat phrases like "kill, stab, slash, and jab," is mandatory for all female students and takes place over five days.

AP McCoy, the champion jockey who has held the title every year since 1997, is urging the nation to support his final Grand National ride with Shutthefrontdoor, with a potential £1 million prize and his retirement hanging in the balance. Reflecting on his career, McCoy acknowledges the unpredictability of the sport but remains hopeful for a fairytale ending. Despite his numerous successes, including winning the Grand National once, McCoy recognizes the challenge ahead and expresses his desire to achieve a second victory for a triumphant conclusion to his record-breaking career.

John Isner advanced to the Miami Open semifinals with a straight-sets victory over Kei Nishikori, becoming the first American man to reach this stage since 2011. In the other semifinal, Andy Murray will face Tomas Berdych, with an interesting dynamic as Berdych is coached by someone who previously worked with Murray. Additionally, tensions between Isner and Nishikori from their previous meeting at the Australian Open are expected to carry over into their match.

Former German football legend Franz Beckenbauer criticized Bayern Munich's performance in their Champions League loss to Porto, comparing it to players taking "sleeping pills." He specifically targeted defender Dante, jokingly calling him a skier, but later apologized for the comment due to Dante's Brazilian background. Beckenbauer expressed doubt about Bayern's ability to progress without significant improvement, despite their domestic success.

A 21-year-old man named Arnold Quintero from San Antonio, Texas, has been arrested for sexually assaulting and physically abusing a 13-year-old girl, who was held captive and subjected to severe violence over several weeks. The girl identified Quintero from a photo lineup and described being punched, forced to undress, and sexually assaulted while also being burned with a lighter. He faces multiple charges including aggravated sexual assault of a child and possession with intent to deliver drugs.

In Week 12 of the Betway Premier League, Michael van Gerwen and Gary Anderson had mixed results, with both winning and losing one game each. Van Gerwen started strong by defeating James Wade 7-0 and securing a spot in the May play-offs, but then lost to Gary Anderson. Anderson, after an initial loss to Stephen Bunting, won a high-scoring match against Van Gerwen with an impressive average of 105.94.

Training consultant Jay Rutland, husband of billionaire heiress Tamara Ecclestone, earned only £65 per week from his company Brigante Business Developments, which reported net assets of £3,378 for the year ending July 2014. Despite his modest income, Rutland and Ecclestone, who were married in a £7 million wedding, enjoy a lavish lifestyle, including a £45 million home and regular extravagant parties for their daughter Sophia. The couple's family life is further enriched by Ecclestone's estimated £3 billion fortune, though Rutland's former career in the City of London ended in 2012 due to market abuse allegations.

A 25-year-old man named Jia Binhui, diagnosed with leukemia in 2013, is using an unconventional home-made treatment involving hot coals to try to cure his cancer, as he cannot afford traditional medical treatment. Jia, from southwest China's Yunnan Province, follows advice from supposed experts that temperatures above 42 degrees Celsius can kill cancer cells and has built a makeshift device in his garden to apply this method. Despite his wife's support, Jia continues this desperate and unproven treatment, hoping it might work before seeking further medical help.

Leroy Fer, a Dutch midfielder for Queens Park Rangers, is set to return to the squad after recovering from a knee injury, potentially for the upcoming match against West Ham. Manager Chris Ramsey is considering Fer despite his limited fitness due to the urgency of the team's position in the relegation battle. Other players are also returning to fitness, including Richard Dunne and Yun Suk-Young, while Rio Ferdinand remains unavailable.

In the final kilometer of the Scheldeprijs race, Team Sky teammates Sir Bradley Wiggins and Geraint Thomas escaped a major crash, while their teammate Elia Viviani was injured, requiring hospital x-rays after hitting the barriers. Team Sky's sports director expressed relief that no other riders were involved in the crash and highlighted that despite the setback, the team remains in good shape for the upcoming Paris-Roubaix race. Alexander Kristoff of Katusha won the race, with only 14 riders competing in the sprint finish.

Before their FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool, Aston Villa's players received supportive messages in their dressing room at Wembley Stadium, including one from fan Mike Shenaniganz Cope encouraging them to "put up with the rain to see the rainbow." Players like Jack Grealish and Brad Guzan shared these messages on social media, with Grealish starting the game and Guzan including a message to "fight like Lions" among others.

A 12-year-old boy named Hanghang in central China suffered severe injuries when his old mobile phone exploded while charging, exposing part of his jawbone and embedding fragments in his arms and legs. Experts attribute such explosions to issues with the battery, improper charging, or other damages, emphasizing the importance of avoiding charging phones while in use and ensuring they are not overcharged. Hanghang, who initially kept quiet about the incident from his parents, is undergoing multiple surgeries to repair his injuries.

Mike Rowe profiles Chad Pregracke, the founder of Living Lands & Waters, on an episode of "Somebody's Gotta Do It," highlighting Pregracke's tireless efforts to clean U.S. waterways. Since 1998, Pregracke and over 87,000 volunteers have collected 8.4 million pounds of trash, earning him the 2013 CNN Hero of the Year Award. To continue his mission in 2015, Pregracke aims to remove an additional 500,000 pounds of trash and invites volunteers to join his cause through LivingLandsAndWaters.org/Get-Involved/.

The ancient Tuscan town of Balestrino, dating back to the 11th century, was abandoned due to seismic instability following several devastating earthquakes, including one in 1887 measuring 6.7 on the Richter scale. Now a ghost town considered the most famous abandoned location in Italy, it has become shrouded in mystery and folklore, with some believing it to be haunted. Drone footage captures the eerie beauty of the deserted town, showing the grand castle and decaying buildings surrounded by nature.

At a special event in Anaheim, California, director J.J. Abrams and the cast of "Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens" premiered the movie's trailer, eliciting gasps, cheers, and applause from the audience. The event showcased the film's live-action sets, introduced the BB8 droid, and teased hints of characters like Luke Skywalker and Princess Leia. The new film, which was filmed on actual sets rather than entirely through CGI, is set to release on December 18.

Former Toronto Mayor Rob Ford announced plans for "very serious" surgery to remove a cancerous tumor in his abdomen, scheduled for May 11th. The tumor, which had shrunk significantly due to chemotherapy and radiation, would be removed by four surgeons over an estimated eight to ten-hour procedure. Ford expressed gratitude for his support system and hoped to return to work in September.

The University of Cape Town in South Africa celebrated the removal of a statue honoring Cecil Rhodes, following weeks of student-led protests that began in March under the hashtag #RhodesMustFall. Opponents argue that Rhodes' legacy is tainted by racism, while some Afrikaner groups and others argue that removing such statues erases history and suppresses dialogue about the past. The debate highlights ongoing tensions over how to address colonial legacies and promote inclusivity in South African institutions and public spaces.

Michael Phelps returned to competitive swimming after a six-month suspension and won the 100 meters butterfly at the Arena Pro Swim Series in Arizona, finishing in 52.38 seconds. The 18-time Olympic gold medalist, who was banned following a drink-driving conviction, expressed joy at being back in competition but will miss the upcoming World Championships in Kazan. Phelps, aiming to compete in a fifth Olympics in Rio de Janeiro, is determined to continue his swimming career.

A woman's body was found hanging from a fire escape in Crown Heights, New York, for over an hour on Sunday morning. Neighbors reported being traumatized by the scene, with one witness initially believing it to be a Halloween prank. The woman, who had known mental health issues, was identified as a social and nice individual by a local resident.

In a thrilling Rhone Valley derby, Lyon secured a 2-2 draw against Saint-Etienne, moving them to the top of Ligue 1 despite playing a man short. Meanwhile, Lille maintained their pursuit of a top-four finish with a 2-0 victory over Bordeaux, keeping within four points of the fourth position. Additionally, Montpellier narrowly defeated Caen 1-0 thanks to an early header from Brazilian defender Hilton, securing their seventh-place standing.

Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger admits he underestimated the contributions of players Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin to the team's recent success in the Premier League. Bellerin, who had limited playing time at Watford, scored a crucial goal against Liverpool, while Coquelin, loaned to Charlton earlier in the season, has become a key player for Arsenal. Wenger praised both players for their performances but noted that Bellerin might have been fortunate to avoid a second yellow card during the match.

Fox is developing a two-hour remake of the cult classic "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" for television, set to celebrate its 40th anniversary. Directed and executive-produced by Kenneth Ortega, the special will feature the original film's producers and will be produced by Fox 21 Television Studios and The Jackal Group. While no premiere date has been announced, the project aims to bring the musical to a new generation of viewers.

Roma FC has been ordered to close part of their stadium for their next home game due to offensive banners displayed by supporters during a recent match against Napoli. These banners, which insulted the mother of a Napoli fan who died in violent clashes, were deemed provocative by a Serie A disciplinary tribunal. In response, club president James Pallotta condemned the fans' actions and emphasized the need for respect and unity in light of the tragic death.

Ellen White scored a spectacular goal for Notts County against her former team, Arsenal, by spinning and firing a free kick into the corner of the goal. This moment was particularly satisfying for White, as it combined scoring against her old team with the successful execution of a well-practiced set-piece from training. Despite this highlight, White later missed a penalty, and the game ended in a draw when Arsenal scored an equalizing goal late in the match.

Arsene Wenger reflects on his decision not to sign Eden Hazard in 2012, stating he has no regrets despite the Belgian star going on to have a standout career at Chelsea. Hazard, now a key player for Chelsea, is considered the frontrunner for the PFA Player of the Year award, although Wenger believes his own forward Alexis Sanchez could also be in contention. Wenger praises Hazard's improved performance, noting his increased maturity and ability to influence games.

Stephen Akers-Belcher, the Mayor of Hartlepool, was dismissed from his care manager role at Newcastle City Council after taking paid leave for a funeral but being photographed on the historic warship HMS Warrior 323 miles away. The council denied he was fired for whistleblowing and stated that an independent investigation found no further action was needed after the police investigation. Akers-Belcher maintained his innocence, stating he had not done anything wrong.

Dr. John Parker, a humanitarian doctor who had been working in an Ebola treatment clinic in Sierra Leone, tested negative for the Ebola virus after developing flu-like symptoms and being taken to Westmead Hospital in Sydney. Dr. Parker had followed protocol and notified authorities upon returning from Sierra Leone. NSW Health confirmed the results, stating that no further testing for the virus was required.

A schoolboy named Frankie Franz, inspired by Barcelona's Martin Montoya, successfully replicated a 27-yard goal into a basketball hoop, surprising both his teammates and family. After watching Montoya perform the trick shot during a training session, nine-year-old Frankie attempted the move at home and scored on his first try, much to the amazement of his mother. The young center midfielder, who dreams of playing for top clubs like Real Madrid or Barcelona, demonstrated remarkable skill and confidence in pulling off this impressive feat.

The Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014 shortlist showcases a diverse range of cricket moments from around the world, including both professional and amateur games. Notably, the winning photograph by Matthew Lewis captures Dwayne Bravo making an incredible full-length catch during the ICC World Twenty20. The collection also features heartwarming and dramatic scenes such as children playing cricket amidst poverty and the world's highest cricket game atop Mount Kilimanjaro.

In a custody dispute, a New Jersey judge ruled that a mother's decision to take her 11-year-old daughter to see Pink perform at a concert was not evidence of bad parenting, despite objections from the father. The judge, after reviewing the case, found that while Pink's performances can be suggestive, they are appropriate for preteens and concluded that the mother acted within reasonable parental judgment. The judge emphasized that the child had a positive experience and was not subjected to any unreasonable risks.

Salcombe, a coastal town in Devon, has surpassed London in average property prices, with the average cost of properties there reaching £671,759, compared to £638,217 in London. Additionally, waterfront properties in Salcombe can cost up to £2 million, exceeding prices in some of London's most expensive neighborhoods such as Notting Hill and Regent's Park. As property values continue to rise, Salcombe is becoming a sought-after destination for those looking to experience a luxurious coastal lifestyle.

Celtic Football Club has criticized the Scottish Football Association (SFA) over the high ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness Caledonian Thistle at Hampden Park. Celtic argue that the North Stand ticket price of £23 is disproportionately high compared to other sections of the stadium and could exclude many supporters. The SFA defended its decision, stating that all four participating clubs were consulted and that the prices have remained the same for the past four years.

A 16-year-old student named Rebecca Rice was allowed to bring her pet Labrador, Holly, into her GCSE French oral exam to help calm her nerves. This unconventional solution was suggested by Rebecca’s teacher, Lorette Esteve, after other common stress-reduction tactics failed. Rebecca spent her five-minute exam period with Holly by her side, which reportedly helped significantly, as she stated that having the dog with her "really settled her nerves."

Anders Lindegaard, the struggling Manchester United goalkeeper, took advantage of the English weather to enjoy a day off with his wife Misse Beqiri. The couple, who tied the knot in a beach wedding in Mauritius and have a son together, shared their happiness through social media. Despite Lindegaard's limited playing time due to competition from other goalkeepers, he remains content off the pitch.

Spanish goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes took a much-needed break from the pressures of the Premier League season by visiting a theme park in England. Their recent form has been impressive, with Manchester United securing six consecutive Premier League wins, including a notable victory over Manchester City, which has boosted their standings and Van Gaal's side's prospects for next season. However, the article also hints at uncertainties regarding their future with the club, given that both players' positions are becoming increasingly competitive.

A 75-year-old piano teacher named John Goodwin, who was on trial for six counts of aggravated felonious sexual assault, shot himself outside the New Hampshire courthouse where his trial was taking place. The victim, now 24, had waited to come forward until 2013 due to embarrassment, alleging repeated assaults by Goodwin. At the time of his suicide, the jury was still deliberating the case.

Amazon removed "Rescue the Anorexia Girl," a controversial mobile game where players throw food at a cartoon anorexic girl, after receiving numerous complaints. The game's creators marketed it as an educational tool to raise awareness about anorexia, but many criticized it for perpetuating harmful stereotypes and potentially harming those with eating disorders. Critics argue that such a game trivializes a serious mental health issue and may discourage individuals from seeking help.

Scientists are working on creating an artificial brain modeled after the European Honeybee's cognitive abilities as part of the Green Brain Project, aiming to develop drones that can think, sense, and act like bees. This project, a collaboration between the Universities of Sheffield and Sussex, has already successfully cloned the vision part of the bee's brain and uploaded it into drones, enabling them to navigate and fly similar to real bees. The ultimate goal is to use these advanced drones for tasks such as crop pollination and search and rescue missions.

A newly-wed Air Malta crew member and her husband were celebrated with a unique post-wedding flight over the Mediterranean, where an Airbus A319 flew in the shape of two giant hearts shortly after takeoff. The unusual flight path was captured by flightradar24.com and was a surprise to many airline enthusiasts, but it was actually a romantic gesture to celebrate the marriage of a pilot and a cabin crew member. At a Norwegian zoo on Easter Monday, a five-year-old giraffe named Melvin died after being gored by an eland antelope in an enclosure. The tragic incident, which occurred when Melvin's head became stuck in the fence, was witnessed by around 30 people, including many children. Despite the quick response of zoo veterinarians, the injuries were too severe, and Melvin succumbed to his wounds shortly after the attack.

A restaurant manager in Leuven, Belgium, sparked outrage after charging a mother 36p to heat up her baby's feeding bottle, leading to a viral Twitter reaction. The mother, Gitte Denteneer, tweeted about the incident, which prompted widespread criticism of the "stingiest boss in Europe." Mexico defended the detention, citing the shipowner's evasion of UN sanctions. Meanwhile, North Korea denied any wrongdoing and claimed that the crew members' human rights were being violated.

Hazel, an English Bulldog puppy, demonstrates her playful and enthusiastic nature in a video where she attempts to balance on and inside a washing basket, eventually causing the basket to tip over and sending her tumbling onto the floor. Catholic bishops in the United States have criticized the BBC drama "Wolf Hall" for its portrayal of historical figures and events, describing it as a "prejudice-laden presentation of the past." The Fort Hood shooting victims are scheduled to receive Purple Heart medals, but some are facing difficulties in obtaining financial support due to the initial classification of the incident as workplace violence rather than terrorism. Staff Sergeant Shawn Manning, who was shot six times, has been denied recognition of his injuries as combat-related, potentially losing out on $800 monthly in benefits and back pay. Newcastle United's head coach, John Carver, describes his role as the most challenging in football due to widespread fan dissatisfaction and a series of poor performances. Despite the club's financial success, including record profits and a large bank balance, fans are boycotting upcoming matches to protest against owner Mike Ashley's management style. Samantha Cameron showcased her "cool" credentials by publicly expressing her admiration for the alternative band Poliça, despite their music's controversial and violent themes. A Welsh couple, Sarah and Mark Brennan, who had endured ten miscarriages over ten years, finally welcomed their daughter Eryn Elisabeth through an unexpected pregnancy and early birth. Moeen Ali is preparing to face Australia's left-arm pacers, Mitchell Johnson and Mitchell Starc, in the upcoming Ashes series, having improved his technique against short balls since his debut in Test cricket. Irish boxer Andy Lee is preparing to defend his WBO middleweight title against former champion Peter Quillin in a fight taking place in New York. Adam Gemili recalls a humorous interaction with Usain Bolt during the 2013 World Championships, where Bolt jokingly challenged Gemili to practice for the 200m despite his focus on the 100m. Gemili credits Bolt's encouragement and advice with helping him perform better in the 200m and aims to build on this support to become a more competitive sprinter.
